evidence.observation: Earlier B close-up shows a small red/orange eye spot at the front of the head.
evidence.distinguishes_because: B's red eye is a visible identity cue; if current X were B, it would need to show this same feature.

evidence.observation: Current X close-up lacks the red/orange eye spot and appears as a dark non-red fish.
evidence.distinguishes_because: This matches earlier A better than B, supporting X=A as in C1.

evidence.observation: Current Y close-up shows a red/orange eye spot similar to B.
evidence.distinguishes_because: Y matches B's red-eye cue; with X not matching B, this supports Y=B and X=A (C1), not the swapped C2.

decision.limitation: Resolution and lighting vary, so the main cue is the visible red eye spot; nearby-time close-ups are used because some 0.0 close-ups are less clear.
